ds: Misuse of lawyers, notaries, accountants and similar professionals, witting or unwitting, to create structures, hold or move client funds, buy assets or lend credibility to transactions. Client accounts and professional privilege are used to distance funds from their source.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Vulnerabilities of Legal Professionals (2013)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach for Legal Professionals (2019)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach for the Accounting Profession (2019)

rat: Lawyers, notaries and accountants run client accounts, form structures and buy assets for clients; fees or deposits sometimes in cash.

ind.n: Client account used with no underlying legal work
ind.cx: Funds pass through client account without a legal service.
ind.ds: A professional's client account is used to move funds with no underlying legal or advisory work.
ind.cn: Professional client account used as pass-through

ind.n: Instructions to transfer funds to third parties without explanation
ind.cx: Sudden redirection of funds to unrelated beneficiaries.
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Complex structures with no commercial reason
ind.cx: Creation of layered entities and trusts.
ind.ds: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
ind.cn: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale

ind.n: Aborted transactions with funds returned elsewhere
ind.cx: Deals cancelled and money sent to different parties.
ind.ds: Deals cancelled and money sent to different parties.

ind.n: Client insists on speed or secrecy
ind.ds: Customer or intermediary urges rapid completion, secrecy or bypassing of checks, or leans on personal connections.
ind.cn: Pressure to speed up or bypass checks

ind.n: Client unwilling to provide ownership or source of funds
ind.cx: Refuses details of beneficial owner or source.
ind.ds: Refuses details of beneficial owner or source.

ind.n: Professional's role unusual for the work
ind.cx: Professional acts as nominee, director, or intermediary beyond normal remit.
ind.ds: Professional acts as nominee, director, or intermediary beyond normal remit.

ind.n: Customer geography far from the professional's practice
ind.cx: No reason to use this adviser.
ind.ds: No reason to use this adviser.

ctl.n: Client money account verification and rules
ctl.ds: Confirms legitimate client-account status and licensing and applies professional client-money rules, alerting on flows lacking a matter reference. It prevents professional accounts being used to move funds without underlying services.

ctl.n: Gatekeeper and company service provider due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses licensing, CDD standards and client mix of formation agents, lawyers and similar professionals and monitors formation volumes and concentration. It targets professional enablers.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Requires a documented commercial or legal reason for each layer of a multi-tier or cross-border structure, with specialist review and sign-off before approval. Unexplained complexity is treated as a risk driver and can lead to decline.

ctl.n: Senior management approval and risk acceptance
ctl.ds: Requires named senior management or a committee to approve onboarding, continuation or waivers for higher-risk relationships, with documented mitigations and periodic re-approval. It adds accountability and an independent challenge to risk acceptance.

Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.
Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

Prohibits or caps cash for purchases, loans, donations and settlement above a set value, requiring documented non-cash methods and threshold reporting for dealers. It removes a low-traceability payment route.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Requires nominee shareholders, directors and signatories to declare their status and name the person they act for, and declines or immobilises bearer instruments. It limits the use of nominees and bearer forms to conceal the real controller.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.
